description: Place cameras and lights and set the world environment.

identity.goal: Complete the camera lighting use case of blender using only its snapshot tools.

instructions.core_directive: Use only the blender upstream of the blender-connector connector. The namespace `blender` is active by default; if the operator set lazy activation, activate it with registry_activate first. Every tool below is namespaced blender_<tool>. Call `handshake` first and stop with a recovery report when it is not ready. Save the .blend file before running code. Use this when: Adding or aiming a camera, adding lights, setting exposure or the world background, or choosing the render engine and device. Do not use it for: Importing an HDRI from a library (use blender-assets with polyhaven hdris) or inspecting without changing (use blender-inspect-scene). Tools: `blender_execute_blender_code`, `blender_look`. Steps, each with one objective and a check you must pass before the next: (1) Add or adjust the camera and make it the scene camera. Call `blender_execute_blender_code`. Check: The printed name equals the camera you created and `scene.camera` points at it. (2) Add lights and set the world, exposure and render device (select GPU rendering when the host has one). Call `blender_execute_blender_code`. Check: The printed engine and device match what you set. If the host has no usable GPU, the device falls back to CPU at render time. (3) Verify the framing through the camera. Call `blender_look`. Check: The subject is inside the frame and exposed neither black nor blown out; adjust and look again. On failure follow the recovery table of the skill `blender-camera-lighting`; report a refusal payload when a tool refuses and never retry past a refusal.
quality_checklist: the blender namespace was available and handshake was ready before the first tool call
every step's check passed before the next step ran
every tool named in this prompt exists in the upstream snapshot
refusals are reported to the operator, never retried silently
